name: Wet Tropics of Queensland
description: This strip of rainforest runs for about 450 km along Queensland's north-east coast, covering roughly 8,940 square kilometres of misty ranges and lowland jungle. It takes up just 0.1% of Australia's land but shelters about half of the country's species. Many of them live nowhere else. Its forests are among the oldest continuously surviving tropical rainforests on Earth, and they hold an unusual concentration of primitive flowering plants.
